title: Devil’s Dream
short: Traditional (British Isles), a favorite  · A 4/4 · play it with every note lit.

blocks.html: A busy reel whose A part rocks back and forth on one high note. Fiddlers play it in A, so banjo players put a capo at the 2nd fret (and raise the 5th string two frets, to A) and play it with G-position fingering: the tab and the chord names are counted from the capo, so they read like G, C and D. Almost every eighth note is a note of the tune. Start slowly; the roll shapes repeat, and so does the tune.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys or strings light up as each note sounds.

blocks.html: The piece: Reel, printed in American fiddle books in the 1800s

sources.name: Melody checked note by note against “Devil’s Dream” in Cole’s 1000 Fiddle Tunes (the 1940 reissue of Ryan’s Mammoth Collection, 1883), as transcribed in ABC by John B. Walsh at MIT’s abc collection (trillian.mit.edu). Played an octave lower; the fiddle’s sixteenth notes are our eighth notes, and the pickups are left out. Every note of that version is in our tab at its time. Chords are ours.
